title: Signficant unnecessary but avoidable allocations when TCP trace enabled at ignored log-level
body:
There are multiple code-paths that follow the pattern:

```
        if (grpc_tcp_trace.enabled()) {
          size_t i;
          for (i = 0; i < tcp->read_slices->count; i++) {
            char* dump = grpc_dump_slice(tcp->read_slices->slices[i],
                                         GPR_DUMP_HEX | GPR_DUMP_ASCII);
            gpr_log(GPR_INFO, ... blah ..., dump);
            gpr_free(dump);
          }
        }
```

where `grpc_dump_slice` builds a nul-terminated string of the fragment; this applies to most network read/write; useful for debugging.

However! If the log-level is low (meaning: less logging - for example ERROR only), but the trace is enabled: this performs a **LOT** of unnecessary CPU and memory overhead, including allocating/releasing the memory for the chunks, and performing hex+ascii dumps - only to have it all ignored by the log-level check.

Proposal: add a log-level test earlier, so that expensive work is not performed for no reason; for example:

```
if (grpc_tcp_trace.enabled() && gpr_should_log(GPR_LOG_SEVERITY_INFO)) // whatever the relevant log-level is
```

or, perhaps more cleanly (but with a new overload):

```
if (grpc_tcp_trace.enabled(GPR_LOG_SEVERITY_INFO)) // whatever the relevant log-level is
```

Candidate scenarios:

- https://github.com/grpc/grpc/blob/c6ebbb5482cf93623a73e54c31277c174c97222f/src/core/lib/iomgr/endpoint_cfstream.cc#L122 (DEBUG)
- https://github.com/grpc/grpc/blob/c6ebbb5482cf93623a73e54c31277c174c97222f/src/core/lib/iomgr/endpoint_cfstream.cc#L229 (DEBUG)
- https://github.com/grpc/grpc/blob/70dd34b4382632b4e668c3d968ca49bb3a67076c/src/core/lib/iomgr/tcp_windows.cc#L364 (INFO)
- https://github.com/grpc/grpc/blob/70dd34b4382632b4e668c3d968ca49bb3a67076c/src/core/lib/iomgr/tcp_windows.cc#L211 (INFO)
- https://github.com/grpc/grpc/blob/32bc9a86562353372968bdf45e13bfeed57b00e8/src/core/lib/security/transport/secure_endpoint.cc#L401 (INFO)
- https://github.com/grpc/grpc/blob/c3c4159d243687a81fe48f32fc91ba061a987c58/src/core/lib/iomgr/tcp_posix.cc#L818 (DEBUG)
- https://github.com/grpc/grpc/blob/c3c4159d243687a81fe48f32fc91ba061a987c58/src/core/lib/iomgr/tcp_posix.cc#L1838 (DEBUG)

However, there may be many more

(aside: this was discovered via the C#/.NET `Grpc.Core` package when using "all" trace and "ERROR" verbosity; in a perfect world, this would be worthy of a bump there, but I do understand the current state of `Grpc.Core`, so I don't know whether that will happen without a fight; I'd like to raise a humble vote for "yay" on that: sadly, not everyone can use the managed version `grpc-dotnet` yet)
